REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - DECEMBER 12, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
DECEMBER 12, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Rick Westra, Trinity Christian Reformed Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Division, BASES Program
  participants at Leal Elementary School – Jake Velazquez, Elli Selassie, Parker Chang,
  and Cameron Lacorte.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  Gonsalves and Leal Elementary Schools (2019 National Blue Ribbon Schools Award).

5B.  Review and consideration of an appointment to the Board of Trustees of the Greater
  Los Angeles County Vector Control District (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to reappoint Mark
  Bollman to serve on the Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District Board of
  Trustees for a four (4) year term commencing January 6, 2020 and expiring on January
  1, 2024 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Albin spoke regarding the City of Cerritos website and inquired regarding the
  security of the existing website format.

  Dipali Patel spoke regarding her coding school franchise in Cerritos.

  Gail Grossman spoke regarding amending the existing sign ordinance regarding the
  placement of political signs.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of
  November 25, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of November 25, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated December 12,
  2019 (COUNCIL).

  Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama recused himself from consideration of Warrant No.
  185434.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Register
  of Demands; with Yokoyama recused from the approval of Warrant No. 185434, as
  follows:

  City of Cerritos  12/12/2019  $3,345,737.80 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period
  ending October 31, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar by Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama for
  separate consideration by the City Council.
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Finance Manager.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, with unanimous approval, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending October 31,
  2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Adoption of Ordinance

  Ordinance introduced at the special meeting of November 25, 2019:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1029, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF CERRITOS AMENDING THE CERRITOS DEVELOPMENT MAP BY CHANGING THE
  ZONE CLASSIFICATION OF APPROXIMATELY ±1.98 ACRES OF LAND, LOCATED AT
  12616 183RD STREET (APN 7030-002-902), FROM OPEN SPACE (OS) TO
  COMMERCIAL OFFICE PROFESSIONAL (COP), HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  DEVELOPMENT MAP AMENDMENT 2017-2 (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar by Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama for
  separate consideration by the City Council.

  A staff report was given by Robert A. Lopez, Current Planning Manager.

  MOTION: A motion was made by Yokoyama, with unanimous approval, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1029, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AMENDING THE CERRITOS DEVELOPMENT MAP BY CHANGING
  THE ZONE CLASSIFICATION OF APPROXIMATELY ±1.98 ACRES OF LAND,
  LOCATED AT 12616 183RD STREET (APN 7030-002-902), FROM OPEN SPACE
  (OS) TO COMMERCIAL OFFICE PROFESSIONAL (COP), HEREIN REFERENCED
  AS DEVELOPMENT MAP AMENDMENT 2017-2 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7E.  Award of a contract for Cerritos arterial street and center median landscape

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to reject the apparent
  low bid and authorize staff to re-bid the contract for Cerritos arterial street and

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt AN URGENCY
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE
  CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES
  (COUNCIL).

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES (COUNCIL).

  Councilmember Pulido recused himself from consideration of this item. He left his
  seat on the dais and exited the City Council Chamber.

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Management Analyst. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Scott Radcliffe, representing the Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce, offered
  the use of the Chamber organization to facilitate further community meetings on
  this topic.

  Ritu Gupta spoke regarding truck noise impacts on Marquardt Avenue.

  Sharun Carlson spoke in support of removing Bloomfield Avenue from the
  established truck routes in Cerritos.

  Faye Ashby noted that trucks are not coming from or going to Cerritos businesses.
  She expressed concern regarding cars with loud exhaust systems adding to the
  noise impacts in the community and requested additional enforcement.

  Sumeet Bidani requested a Citywide truck noise study, additional enforcement of
  truck route ordinances, and expressed concern regarding the safety of the bicycle
  path on Carmenita Road.

  Janis Fok spoke in opposition to the proposed ordinance, as the proposed route will
  pass two schools located near Shoemaker Road; suggested the route instead be
  directed to Valley View; and requested additional crossing guard resources.

  Trina Norman, representing United Parcel Service, spoke in opposition to the
  proposed truck route ordinance and noted the company is interested in
  collaborating with the City. She stated the proposed truck route will adversely
  impact UPS operations.
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Suzanne Neal spoke in support of the removing Bloomfield from the existing truck
  route ordinance.

  Billie Medina spoke in support of the proposed ordinance.

  Ruby Martinez thanked the City Council for listening to residents and spoke in
  support of the proposed ordinance.

  Sam Chu spoke in opposition to the proposed ordinance and suggested vetting the
  number of trucks per business to minimize the noise.

  Jane Arellano spoke in support of removing Bloomfield from the existing truck
  route ordinance and noted that Sundance townhomes do not have a buffer wall,
  such as many other residences in the area, adding to the noise impact in that
  community.

  Peggy Paddock spoke in support of the proposed ordinance.

  Chris Cascone expressed gratitude for the study, spoke in support of removing
  Bloomfield from the existing truck route ordinance and spoke regarding the
  impacts of the construction on the 5 freeway.

  Dale Woods thanked the City Council for authorizing the study, spoke in support of
  removing Bloomfield from the existing truck route ordinance, and expressed
  concern regarding truck noise.

  Charles Jordan spoke in support of removing Bloomfield from the existing truck
  route ordinance and noted the quality of life concerns related to truck noise on
  Bloomfield.

  Chris Aafedt spoke in support of removing Bloomfield from the existing truck route
  ordinance and suggested routing trucks toward Alondra Boulevard as an
  alternative.

  John A. L. Moran spoke in opposition the proposed ordinance, requesting that truck
  routes not be located on 166th Street and that traffic be slowed down on Bloomfield
  Avenue.

  Jackie Bayer expressed concerns regarding enforcement of existing truck route
  ordinances and the added pollution the trucks exude.

  Denoris Baker spoke in opposition of the proposed ordinance, expressing concerns
  of truck noise stating the trucks are passing between 1:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m.,
  causing significant sleep deprivation.

  Sean Wallace, representing United Parcel Service, spoke in opposition of the
  proposed ordinance, requesting collaboration with the City to ensure a positive
  outcome for all interested parties.

  De Angelo Gomez, representing United Parcel Service, spoke in opposition, noting
  that the proposed ordinance does not address the community’s safety concerns and
  requested exemptions for resident businesses from truck route ordinance
  restrictions.
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Bob Jordan, representing United Parcel Service, spoke in opposition to the
  proposed ordinance, expressing that safety is paramount to the UPS company,
  noted that the proposed ordinance will hinder UPS operations, and requested
  exemptions for UPS from the truck route ordinance restrictions.

  Mario Archaga, representing United Pacel Service, spoke in opposition to the
  proposed ordinance, requesting exemptions for UPS from the truck route ordinance
  restrictions and for collaboration with the City on solutions, asking the City
  consider the ordinance after the holiday season.

  Sophia Tse, ABCUSD Boardmember, spoke in opposition to the proposed ordinance,
  and expressed concerns regarding safety issues related to large trucks, the times
  the study was conducted and the additional pollution exuded by large trucks.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding enforcement of truck route ordinances and
  regarding safety of the students in the community.

  Jose Chavez spoke in support of the proposed ordinance stating that it does not
  affect or apply to UPS trucks but that root of the truck problems are from the
  distribution center at Bloomfield Avenue and Rosecrans Avenue.

  Chandan Bisht spoke in opposition of the proposed ordinance, noting that the City
  should have sent notifications regarding the truck route ordinance amendment to
  all Whitney High School students and Wittmann Elementary School students.

  Peter Barton spoke in support of the proposed ordinance, noting that the problem
  is not with UPS trucks, but the large container trucks.

  Karla Cedillo spoke in opposition of the proposed ordinance, noting that moving
  truck routes to Shoemaker is just moving the problem, but not creating a real
  solution.

  Miguel Garcia spoke in support of the proposed ordinance, noting that he requested
  solutions to the truck noise problem in 2005 and received a response from Mayor
  Crawley but did not receive mitigation to the problem.

  Lin expressed concerns regarding truck traffic on Carmenita Road and for the
  safety of the students at the schools adjacent to the street, noting that moving
  traffic to Shoemaker Avenue is a relocation of the existing problem.

  Sally Havice spoke in support of the proposed ordinance, expressing concerns
  regarding the ramifications of the vehicle pollutants. She noted the proposed route
  does not pass in front of schools and stated an exemption for UPS would be
  acceptable.

  Sun Yi Kim spoke in support of the proposed ordinance, expressing concerns
  regarding the noise and sleep deprivation caused by large trucks passing on
  Bloomfield Avenue.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama stated his opposition to the addition of the truck route on
  Shoemaker Avenue.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1030, AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Pulido (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to waive full reading of
  and introduce Ordinance No. 1031, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 10.18 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUCK ROUTES (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Pulido (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  At the conclusion of this item, Councilmember Pulido returned to the City Council
  Chamber and resumed his seat on the dais.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Pine Tree Reforestation Program for
  residential parkways (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Maheekanth Murakonda spoke in support of the program and of the cost of keeping
  pine trees over an extended period of time and noted that six months have passed
  since he was promised by the City that his tree will be removed as soon as possible.

  Jennifer Hong thanked the City Council and staff for taking action regarding this
  issue and expressed concern regarding residents removing their own trees.

  John A. L. Moran expressed concern regarding the intentions of the original City plan
  for the pine trees and inquired as to whether the original plan will be enforced when
  new trees are planted.

  Celia Spitzer spoke regarding the proposed plan’s expedition of the removal of the
  canary pine trees and noted that many residents do not desire removal of the trees.
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 8 of 10

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Approve the final draft of the City of Cerritos, Pine Tree Reforestation Program for
  Residential Parkways; and

  2. Allocate the necessary funds of $341,000 to contract with a vendor and complete the
  removal of approximately fifty residential parkway pine trees by the end of Fiscal
  Year 2019-2020; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute the necessary change orders to current Public
  Works construction and maintenance contacts in order to complete year one of the
  Cerritos Pine Tree Reforestation Program for Residential Parkways (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a request by the La Palma-Cerritos Branch of the
  American Association of University Women for use of the City Council Chamber to
  conduct a candidate forum relating to the March 3, 2020 Cerritos General Municipal
  Election (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting no individuals elected to speak, the
  Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the request by
  the La Palma-Cerritos branch of the American Association of University Women for use
  of the City Council Chamber on Monday, February 3, 2020 from 6:30 p.m. to 9:30
  p.m. to conduct a candidate forum relating to the March 3, 2020 Cerritos General
  Municipal Election and waive associated City costs (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an award of a contract for the preparation of design
  and construction documents as well as environmental studies as required by State
  and Federal law in support of the Del Amo Boulevard bridge replacement and
  signal enhancements project, RFP No. 1370-19 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  December 12, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 9 of 10

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Joan Pylman expressed support for the bridge replacement and signal
  enhancements project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Award a professional services contract in the amount of $3,420,800 to Kimley-
  Horn and Associates for the preparation of design and construction documents,
  environmental studies/documents as required by State and Federal law in
  compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and National
  Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and seek funding for construction as related
  to the Del Amo Boulevard Bridge Replacement and Signal Enhancements
  Project, RFP No. 1370-19; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager and/or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders required to facilitate the completion of the project (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  None.

  None.

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Pulido, Hu, and Edwards, Mayor Pro

  None.

  The meeting adjourned at 11:28 p.m.
